name: review-3471
description: Defer argument redaction by storing indices instead of rewriting argv
author: rjd15372

maintainer_comments.author: zuiderkwast
maintainer_comments.body:
A dynamic array with 16 bytes overhead in the client struct seems overkill.

The arguments we redact are always among the first 32 or 64 arguments, right? We can use a bitmap instead, where each bit represents an argument index, 1 means redact, 0 means don't redact. Args beyond the fixed number can't be redacted. Seems safe to me.


```suggestion
    uint32_t redact_arg_bitmap; /* Bitmap of argument indexes that should be redacted in logs. */
```

maintainer_comments.author: zuiderkwast
zuiderkwast
maintainer_comments.body:
> On the other hand, this assert might trigger if someone runs a very long ACL SETUSER ... command with many rules.

Yeah, if it's variadic, it's a real problem.

We can let the 0-bit mean all args above 31 should be redacted. No need to encode a specific index, is it?

maintainer_comments.author: zuiderkwast
maintainer_comments.body: Or just when it redacts any arg > 31, we set the flag and imply redacting all args > 31.
